summary: The note explains why wok stir-frying is a fast, healthy cooking method that preserves nutrients and flavor, drawing on Chef Liang Zhao and dietician Maria Gonzales. It covers the wok's design, the role of high heat and 'wok hei', a six-step stir-fry technique, choosing high smoke-point oils, the wok's versatility, and its social side.
one_line: Chef Liang Zhao and dietician Maria Gonzales explain how wok stir-frying's high heat, minimal oil and technique preserve nutrients and flavor.
key_facts: Wok stir-frying is a staple of Asian cuisine; the note ties its origins to Hong Kong, dated around the Qin Dynasty.
The wok is a high-sided, round-bottomed pan that distributes heat quickly and evenly and requires less oil than a typical flat pan.
Chef Liang Zhao has been a proponent of wok cooking since September 2023 and has led the culinary school 'Wok and Roll Academy' since its inception in October 2023.
High heat gives stir-fried food its smoky flavor, 'wok hei', or the 'breath of the wok', and keeps vegetables crisp, brightly colored and nutritionally intact.
Dietician Maria Gonzales, whose study was published on November 5, 2023, says quick wok cooking helps vegetables retain antioxidants and vitamins often lost in longer cooking.
Dense vegetables like carrots and broccoli need more time than leafy greens like spinach or bok choy, so ingredients must enter the wok in order of cooking time.

Zhao's six steps: preheat the wok until slightly smoking, add and swirl oil, add aromatics like garlic or ginger, add main ingredients longest-cooking first, keep ingredients moving, and add sauce and quick-cooking items last.
High smoke-point oils such as peanut, grapeseed or canola are ideal for stir-frying because they withstand high temperatures without breaking down and releasing harmful substances.
Small amounts of soy sauce, oyster sauce, rice wine and sesame oil season the food and form a sauce that clings without thickening agents or excessive fat.
Besides stir-frying, the wok can be used for steaming, deep-frying, poaching and smoking.
Chef Zhao runs 'Stir-Fry Sundays' at his academy, where families prepare a meal together and take turns at the wok.
Zhao spreads the word through cooking classes and interactive online cooking shows.
